stories.headline: US-Iran attacks on oil tankers push crude prices above $100 a barrel

sources.body:
Oil prices rose past $100 a barrel on Wednesday after an overnight escalation in the conflict between the US and Iran.

In back and forth attacks, the US hit five Iranian tankers in reprisal strikes after Tehran targeted one of its warships.

Brent crude - which is the global benchmark for prices - has not been as expensive since the end of July, when a ceasefire between Iran and the US collapsed .

It did dip back down to $99.90 a barrel, but any fresh flare-ups in the Middle East could see it pushed higher again.

The US strikes on the five Iranian tankers saw four in the Gulf of Oman linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) hit as well as another near Kharg Island.

Tehran responded by launching missiles at a US base in Jordan - most of which were shot down - and said it attacked two US vessels and eight oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil prices have fluctuated wildly during the war, which started on 28 February this year.

Before the conflict Brent crude had been priced at about $70 (£52) a barrel.

But the war saw the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which carries 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The rising costs have sparked huge price leaps in petrol around the world for motorists at the pumps .

Tit-for-tat strikes between Iran and the US have escalated in the past week, more than six months after the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on 28 February..

Jordan said it had shot down 18 of the 20 Iranian missiles, while two of them fell in unpopulated areas, an official spokesperson for the Jordanian Armed Forces said.

After warning of further retaliatory strikes, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday they had attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers and 10 "non-compliant vessels" trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, state media reported.

The latest round of escalation comes after Iran targeted a US warship with ballistic missiles, which Centcom said were "successfully evaded". It added that no American troops were harmed during the attacks.

In response, the US said that the five Iranian oil tankers it targeted were "part of a multi-billion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies".

One of the ships it had struck, the M/T Riesco, sunk in the Gulf of Oman, Centcom later said, posting a video on X of the damaged vessel.

Kharg Island - where one Iranian tanker was attacked in the latest round of US strikes - hosts Iran's main terminal for exporting oil.

Some 90% of the country's crude oil passes through the island in the Gulf, transported through pipes from the mainland.

Pressure on oil prices has been exacerbated by wider regional instability.

Also on Tuesday, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement attacked energy facilities and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, injuring 73 people, according to Saudi authorities.

The drone and missile attack caused fires at oil facilities and installations that led to a temporary halt in operations, Saudi Arabia's military and energy ministry said.
sources.headline: Oil hits $100 a barrel for first time since July after flare up in US-Iran conflict

sources.body:
Tit-for-tat violence surges again in region, with tankers struck by the US in the Gulf of Oman, and reprisal attacks by Iran on a US base in Jordan

The US military on Tuesday said it had “destroyed” several Iranian tankers after Iran attempted to strike a US navy warship with ballistic missiles, as violence once again surged across the region, pushing the price of oil past $100 a barrel.

American forces struck the tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Iran’s Kharg Island, US central command (Centcom) said in a statement, adding that American forces “directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck”.

Centom said the strikes came after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days. “The US warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed,” it said in a statement.

The IRGC said they had struck a US military base in Jordan in retaliation. Air-defence systems destroyed 18 ⁠of the ⁠20 ​ballistic missiles originating ⁠from Iranian territory, Jordan’s state ⁠news ​agency ‌reported, citing the ‌armed forces, adding that two missiles fell in unpopulated areas ‌and there were no casualties.

The IRGC also said they ⁠attacked ⁠two US ​vessels and eight ⁠oil tankers in the Gulf, after warning crews of oil tankers near ports in Kuwait and Bahrain to immediately leave their vessels.

After a month of relative calm in August, Iran and the US have resumed exchanges of fire, sending ‌global oil prices back up to levels last seen in July. On Wednesday, oil prices rose above $100 a barrel in early Asia trading.

On Tuesday, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in Saudi Arabia , wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a significant expansion of the Middle East war.

Saudi Arabia said it would retaliate after the strikes – reportedly involving dozens of drones and missiles – that targeted several oil facilities in the country’s south.

Remarking on the latest strikes by Iran, Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, said the US would not let Iran’s attacks to go unanswered.

“Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships. And for every time they do that or try to do that, they’re going to lose tankers. And I think you’ll see that again today,” Rubio said on Tuesday, during a trip to Colombia.

The strikes followed an earlier dispute over an American underwater drone in the strait of Hormuz, which the IRGC claimed to have seized as part of a “complex intelligence and operational action at dawn”, according to Iranian state TV. In a statement, the IRGC said images of the vessel would be released shortly.

In a statement, US Navy Capt Tim Hawkins, a United States Centcom spokesperson, said the submersible was “defective” and an older model “that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment”. Operations in the area continue, he said.

sources.body:
US military says it struck the five Iranian tankers after IRGC targeted a US warship twice in two days.

US bombs five Iranian oil tankers after its navy is attacked

The United States has attacked five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island after accusing Tehran of launching ballistic missiles at a US warship twice in two days.

Iran responded to Tuesday’s attacks by firing missiles at US forces stationed at the Al Azraq base in Jordan. It also claimed additional strikes on at least two US vessels and eight tankers in the region, saying the assaults caused “great damage”.

The exchange of fire comes amid escalating tensions in the Gulf six months into the US and Israel’s war on Iran, with Tehran closing the Strait of Hormuz and Washington enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

The hostilities drove oil prices to $99.49 a barrel in early trading on Wednesday.

In a statement late on Tuesday, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had sought to target a US warship twice over the past two days, but that the vessel “successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks”.

“No American personnel were harmed,” it said.

CENTCOM said it responded by striking and destroying the Iranian oil carriers, M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman, as well as M/T Derya near Kharg Island.

“American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable,” CENTCOM added.

It later published a video that it said showed the M/T Riesco sinking in the Gulf of Oman.

Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster confirmed the attack near Kharg Island, which handled some 90 percent of the country’s oil exports before the war. It reported that the crew was evacuated and said a second tanker was hit near the southern port of Jask in the Gulf of Oman.

The IRGC later said that five tankers were targeted.

It said it retaliated by subjecting Al Azraq base in Jordan to “fierce missile strikes” and claimed that hangars used by US fighter jets were destroyed in the attacks.

The IRGC went on to claim ballistic missile attacks on the US Navy DDG-119 and DDG-53 destroyers, saying the strikes caused “significant damage… to these vessels”.

In a subsequent statement, it said its naval forces targeted “2 American vessels and 8 tankers in the region, causing great damage to them”. It was not clear if the two “American vessels” were the same destroyers mentioned in the earlier statement.

There was no immediate comment from the US on the Iranian claims.

The ship attacks followed a statement by the IRGC that warned of imminent attacks on oil tankers in Bahrain and Kuwait’s borders. The IRGC said all crews must evacuate immediately.

Jordan’s Armed Forces, meanwhile, said the country’s air defences engaged 20 ballistic missiles, “successfully intercepting and destroying 18 of them”. Two missiles “fell in unpopulated areas”, it said in a statement.

The attacks did not cause any casualties, and specialised teams “have begun securing the locations where debris and shrapnel fell”, the military added.

stories.headline: Britain, France and Canada move to ban imports from Israeli West Bank settlements

sources.body:
Ed Miliband announces sanctions on trade with settlements as PM says in the Guardian it is time to act

I believe in a two-state solution in the Middle East. That’s why we’re taking action to keep that hope alive | Andy Burnham

Settler terrorists supported by Benjamin Netanyahu’s government are committing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, Ed Miliband has said, in the UK’s starkest condemnation since the foundation of the Israeli state.

Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act , “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”.

In the Commons, the foreign secretary said the government would now take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety, as he announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements.

The dramatic shift in the UK’s position comes after a summer of intense diplomacy against a backdrop of increasing settler violence in the West Bank, which has resulted in 12 nations – including France and Canada – announcing they would impose sanctions.

In a joint statement Burnham, Emmanuel Macron and Mark Carney said: “The time has come to take further action to uphold our commitment to protect the two-state solution, our interests and to stand up for our values, before it is too late.”

In response, the Israeli foreign minister, Gideon Saar, announced the closure of the UK consulate in Jerusalem and that 12 British MPs and activists – including Jeremy Corbyn and Labour MP Diane Abbott – would be banned from entering Israel .

Saar accused Miliband of “outrageous lies” and said the UK government was “systematically working against the state of Israel”. Washington’s ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, warned that the US could take retaliatory action over trade.

However, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said Washington would “obviously” not follow the UK’s course of action, and did not want to see the West Bank destabilised, but declined to comment further. Burnham had briefed Donald Trump on the plan in advance.

In his statement to parliament, Miliband said the UK government would enact:

An import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories and a new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.

A comprehensive sanctions regime against providing services such as construction or financing for Israeli settlements and a ban on advertising them in the UK.

Personal sanctions against key individuals accused of promoting settler violence.

A new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.

The foreign secretary said the UK’s actions would show that “Britain is not silent in the face of deep injustice, and nor is it powerless”. In an emotional statement, he described the agony he had heard from Palestinians in the West Bank whose homes had been destroyed and from doctors in Gaza who had seen children dying waiting for medical treatment.
sources.headline: UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing

sources.body: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
sources.headline: UK, France, Canada to ban imports from Israeli settlements

sources.body:
Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said the ban represents a ‘comprehensive reset’ of the UK’s policy on Israel.

The United Kingdom has announced a ban on the import of all goods produced by illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the country’s most significant policy since London’s historic recognition of Palestinian statehood last year.

In a speech to Parliament, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accused Israel of carrying out “ethnic cleansing” in Palestine and affirmed that it is official UK policy that the Israeli settlements rapidly expanding across the occupied West Bank are “unlawful”.

He said he did not believe “the British people want us supporting the occupation by accepting products from settlements in our shops”.

Miliband also announced tougher new restrictions on arms sales to Israel.

Israel announced four “counter measures”, including banning 12 British MPs from entering Israel and closing the British consulate in Jerusalem, following his speech.

The UK’s trade ban on goods from illegal settlements comes amid an intensifying wave of Israeli settler pogroms on Palestinian communities in the occupied West Bank and controversial settlement expansions that have prompted a UK-led debate on Europe-wide trade restrictions.

After Miliband’s speech, 12 countries shared a joint statement supporting the two-state solution and announcing their own intentions to impose restrictions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements.

France, the UK, Canada, Denmark, Spain, Finland, Ireland, Iceland, Norway, Poland, Portugal and Sweden called on the Israeli government to immediately halt the expansion of settlements.

Ahead of Tuesday’s announcement, Miliband said new trading bans and sanctions would represent a “comprehensive reset” of the UK’s policy on Israel, amounting to an approach that “not only calls out the injustice [in Palestine], but acts”.

However, he added: “The sanctions regime will target illegal settlements and settlement expansion, not Israel.”

“I can also announce that we’re extending the existing global human rights regime such that it will enable swifter action to deter settlement expansion, including crucially seeking to prevent the development of E1 ,” Miliband added. E1, a proposed settlement in the West Bank, would divide the Palestinian territory in two and put an end to hopes for a two-state solution, he said.

In support of Israel, Miliband also announced new sanctions against the financing arm of the Lebanese group Hezbollah – Al-Qard al-Hasan – and said the UK will reimpose sanctions on Iran, in line with those imposed by the European Union and United States.

However, he said the UK government “agrees” that settler violence in areas of the West Bank amounts to ethnic cleansing and labelled those carrying it out as “settler terrorists”. He accused the Israeli government of turning a blind eye to the violence and intimidation of Palestinians.

Miliband reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to a two-state solution for Palestine and sharply criticised the rhetoric of Israeli politicians, such as Minister of Finance Bezalel Smotrich, who have called for an end to any notion of a Palestinian state.

stories.headline: UK air-traffic-control failure leaves widespread flight disruption

sources.body:
Kevin Peachey Cost of living correspondent

It looks like it could be another frustrating day for air passengers, and many will be unsure about their rights.

On one level, it's quite simple. If your flight is cancelled, your airline is still obliged to get you to your destination, even if it is on another carrier, or give you a refund.

For delays, you may have the right to food, or a hotel stay, depending on the length of the wait.

When delays and cancellations are the fault of an airline, then passengers may be entitled to extra compensation. But, clearly, air traffic control issues are beyond the control of airlines, so no extra payments will be made.

Experts are urging passengers to check the advice from your airport, tour operator, and airline apps on a regular basis.
sources.headline: More UK flights delayed as air traffic control boss apologies for widespread disruption

sources.body:
Martin Rolfe, who faces pressure to resign, due to brief Heidi Alexander after cancellations pass 1,900

How have you been affected by UK air traffic disruption?

The boss of the air traffic control provider Nats has been summoned to meet the UK transport secretary as the number of flight cancellations passed 1,900 in a second day of disruption for hundreds of thousands of passengers.

Martin Rolfe, who is facing increasing pressure to resign over a third major stoppage to flights in just over three years, is due to brief Heidi Alexander on Wednesday.

Those delayed included thousands of passengers left stuck on grounded planes for many hours as the incident unravelled, and others stranded overnight at airports abroad.

Airlines including Ryanair and Wizz called for Rolfe to resign or be sacked by Alexander.

Rolfe ruled out a cyber-attack as a cause for the “technical issue” at air traffic control and defended the resiliency of the systems run by Nats, which provides services to 15 UK airports.

“We will be doing a very thorough and full investigation,” he told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. “We have at this point ruled out a cyber-attack.

“I don’t believe we have ever seen an incident happen more than once. This will be something we haven’t seen in more than 50 years of operation. I would say the UK has one of the best reputations in the world both from a safety perspective and resilience perspective.”

Nats said the problem occurred in its flight processing system but was not the same fault as those that caused outages and mass disruption in 2023 and 2025.

However, Ryanair queried the explanation and said lessons had not been learned. The carrier, which on Tuesday said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted when 50 flights were cancelled, said it had now cancelled more than 250 flights and its costs would run into millions.

Ryanair’s chief operations officer, Neal McMahon, said the airline had been told the issue had occurred in the flight processing system again.

“Airlines across the UK cancelled over a thousand flights, and hundreds of thousands of people were disrupted because the lessons learned for the previous failures have not been delivered by Martin Rolfe,” he told Times Radio.

McMahon added: “We’re told yesterday this was a spurious flight plan which caused the same outage and our question is like: ‘These things can happen, but where’s the backup systems?’”

The airline, Europe’s biggest carrier, had earlier urged Alexander and Nats’ board to “stop making excuses for repeated Nats failures and appoint a new leader capable of running the UK ATC system”.

Yvonne Moynihan, the managing director of Wizz Air UK, called on Rolfe to consider resigning over the repeated technical failures at Nats.

“In any industry when you’ve had three failures, you need to consider three strikes and you’re out,” she told Today.

“A third time and a third excuse is not enough any more. What we need to see from leadership is accountability. There are serious questions about the resilience of the system. I think Nats and the leadership need to look deep inside themselves.”
sources.headline: Nats boss summoned by UK transport secretary as flight chaos enters second day

sources.body: Flights from British airports began to resume Wednesday after a glitch in the country's air traffic control service left hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded. Authorities warned that travellers would continue to experience delays as airlines scrambled to recover from the outage.

stories.headline: US bans Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorcycle imports as trade dispute escalates

sources.body:
The US will ban imports of a range of Canadian products, including alcoholic spirits, some dairy goods and motorbikes, after its neighbour's retaliatory tariffs on American goods came into force.

In a series of executive orders on Tuesday, President Donald Trump said Canada was "discriminating" against the US and outlined the bans, which will begin on 29 September.

Officials on both sides have said they would like to strike a trade deal, but no new talks have been scheduled since negotiations collapsed in late August.

Dominic LeBlanc, Canada's trade minister, said the latest US measures were "unjustified" and that he would work to protect the country's workers, families and businesses.

"Our core focus is on what we can control: building strength at home, diversifying our partnerships abroad, and building Canada strong for all Canadians," LeBlanc said.

He said he had contacted his US counterpart and promised to work "in good faith" to resolve tensions.

Earlier on Tuesday, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a video address that his country's move away from the US as its largest trading partner "will come at a cost".

The White House's new sanctions are the latest strike in a months-long trade war between the US and Canada. The two countries have historically been close allies, with each a key business partner to the other.

Generally more than two-thirds of Canada's total exports go to the US. In 2025, Canada's exports of alcoholic spirits to the US were worth US$687m (£507m), dairy products were worth $269m and motorbikes were worth $90m, according to UN data compiled by Trading Economics.

Canada is the second-largest trading partner of the US after Mexico, although its exports are far more diversified than Mexico's.

In recent months, business owners on both sides of the border have expressed fears over the trade war's fallout . Many expect prices of goods to rise and the number of customers to fall.

Last month, the White House imposed 50% tariffs on around $20bn (£14.8bn) of Canadian goods after several rounds of talks had broken down.

Those tariffs hit sectors including Canada's furniture and wine industries, as well as some sporting and fishing equipment businesses.

Canada responded with what Carney called "dollar-for-dollar" tariffs on US goods like steel, clothing and furniture. The counter-duties came into effect after midnight on Tuesday.

Canada is "discriminating" against US businesses by restricting American goods while not doing the same to the same products from other countries, the White House said when announcing the new import restrictions on Tuesday.

Some products, like whey and non-alcoholic beer, have been banned from import entirely, while tariffs have been further hiked for others, including for cheeses and cheese substitutes - which were not covered by bans - and for motorboats.

stories.headline: OpenAI claims breakthrough on a difficult mathematics problem, prompting questions from rival researchers

sources.body:
OpenAI says it has found a solution to a decades-old advanced maths problem in a matter of hours using a new artificial intelligence (AI) model and thousands of AI bots.

The ChatGPT-maker said on Tuesday that by focusing a group of roughly 10,000 AI agents, or AI bots that undertake tasks somewhat autonomously, it solved a notoriously difficult maths problem in just 88 hours.

The problem was part of the Navier-Stokes equations , which concern how fluids move. For 90 years important aspects of the problems have lacked a proof, the argument underlying a correct math equation.

OpenAI called the solution which it found a "milestone" and evidence that AI tools are improving quickly.

OpenAI's solution has yet to be verified independently or publicly accepted by The Clay Mathematics Institute, a maths organisation based in the US which runs the Millennium Prize that offers big money to the first to solve certain mathematical conundrums.

But the company's claim has already sparked a backlash.

Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematics professor at New York University, said on Tuesday that he and Levent Alpöge, a mathematician working for OpenAI rival Anthropic , had also been working on solving the problem.

The duo had been using OpenAI's tool Codex in their work. But Buckmaster said that on 3 September, he found out that "information about our progress had been passed to OpenAI".

Buckmaster's statement came the same day, but hours before, OpenAI published its Navier–Stokes work. He claimed that OpenAI did not begin working on the Navier–Stokes equations until "after information about our work had reached OpenAI". He included text from emails exchanged with OpenAI over the work and his questions of the company's timing and methods.

Buckmaster added that he had not yet read OpenAI's full proof, but felt compelled to go public with "what I was told, when, and what was proposed to me...because the alternative is to let a sequence of announcements say something I know to be false".

OpenAI on Tuesday congratulated the "concurrent work" of Buckmaster and Alpöge, calling it "remarkable".

The company said it had not seen "any of their work through any means until they released it publicly" and that no user data was accessed in its work on the Navier–Stokes problem.

"While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models⁠", the company added. "However, our proofs differ significantly and even the precise results proved are different."

OpenAI said that, at the end of August, it started to train a new model that quickly showed that it was adept at maths. AI models are computer programs trained on huge amounts of data to recognise and predict patterns in information.

While the new OpenAI model remains a tool only used within the company, as it is "significantly more capable" than the company's most recent AI model release, its researchers decided to use it on certain notable advanced maths problems.

OpenAI admitted that last week on 1 September, it had "heard rumours that two Millennium Prize problems had been resolved" and so decided to put thousands of AI bots trained on the new internal model to work attempting to solve some of the remaining problems.
sources.headline: OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours

sources.body: US tech giant OpenAI on Tuesday said it had solved one of the hardest problems in mathematics with an unreleased artificial intelligence model after just 88 hours – and millions of dollars' worth of computing power. But a US mathematician and a researcher at rival Anthropic allege that OpenAI only took up the problem after it had gotten wind of their own AI-assisted efforts to crack the challenge which had demanded months to craft a radically distinctive approach.
sources.headline: OpenAI says its models solved one of math's hardest problems as researchers cry foul

JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. (AP) — Dueling court orders eight weeks before Election Day left Missouri’s congressional map uncertain Tuesday as legal wrangling over a redistricting plan backed by President Donald Trump sparked fresh confusion.
sources.headline: Competing court orders add confusion to Missouri congressional elections

sources.body: A Republican-led bid to revive a redistricting plan that favors the GOP fell short at the Supreme Court Tuesday, but it later picked up steam after a federal judge in Missouri ruled that officials must move ahead with the districts used in primaries last month — a map that’s likely to net Republicans an additional House seat. Justice Brett Kavanaugh turned down a Republican-backed emergency appeal that sought to block a Missouri Supreme Court ruling last week restoring earlier district lines and ordering that voters to weigh in on the redistricting plan in November for use in future elections. However, Chief U.S. District Court Judge Stephen Clark, in a decision made public within minutes of Kavanaugh’s ruling, issued a temporary restraining order that effectively set aside the state Supreme Court’s decision and granted Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins’ request to move forward with the plan likely to elect a Republican in one of the state’s two districts currently held by Democrats. The Democratic group leading the push to block Republicans' redistricting efforts swiftly appealed Clark's decision to the 8th Circuit Court and asked the court for an emergency temporary stay while it considers the appeal. The group has asked Clark to stay his order, and it also asked Missouri's Supreme Court to hold Hoskins in contempt. The dissonant rulings add another layer of chaos to Missouri’s election administration. Local election officials had prepared for months as the debate over which map to use moved through the court system, planning for elections in the event either map gets used. The state used the new, gerrymandered map for August’s primaries. The timing of settling these legal disputes is crucial. The rulings came hours before the Tuesday deadline for Missouri election officials to make changes to any ballots, and ballots must be finalized before ballots begin to be sent out on Sept. 19. Hoskins sent an email to election officials Tuesday evening directing them to comply with Clark's order and prepare for November's election under the gerrymandered map, according to Democrats' filing Tuesday evening to the Missouri Supreme Court. Kavanaugh issued his ruling because he handles urgent matters arising in the 8th Circuit, which includes Missouri. Kavanaugh issued no explanation of his decision, nor did he indicate that he had referred the matter to the full court, as is customary in significant cases. Missouri officials could ask another justice for relief, but such requests are almost never granted. The justices rarely disturb state courts’ decisions about matters like the referendum petitions in Missouri that sought to put the redistricting before voters for approval. Clark, a St. Louis-based Trump appointee, said two Republican candidates who sued were likely to prevail in their arguments that changing the district lines at this point in the process would violate two provisions in the U.S. Constitution: one establishing the House of Representatives and another guaranteeing equal protection of the laws. Lawyers for state officials warned in their appeal to the Supreme Court that the state faced “disaster” and “unprecedented chaos” in part because primaries already took place under the new lines last month. Democrats argued any last-minute chaos to Missouri’s election administration was intentionally created by Hoskins, pointing to Republican leaders in the state arguing that delaying the decision on the redistricting referendum would benefit Republicans. President Donald Trump denounced the state Supreme Court ruling last week. “The Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America!" he wrote in a post on Truth Social . “Missouri must be able to use the map that was in effect just a couple of months ago, in the Primary. This is a Dark Day for “Justice” in Missouri!”

stories.headline: Stefany Shaheen wins New Hampshire Democratic House primary

sources.body: The Shaheen political dynasty lives on in New Hampshire. Stefany Shaheen, the eldest daughter of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), won Tuesday’s hotly contested Democratic primary for the state’s 1st District, defeating Maura Sullivan and a host of other rivals despite facing attacks that she was leaning on her well-known surname. The seat, left open by Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas when he opted to run for Senate, is considered to be fairly competitive for the general election — former Vice President Kamala Harris won it by just two points in 2024. Shaheen attempted to create distance from her mother throughout her campaign, rebuking the deal the senator helped broker to end last fall’s government shutdown and leaning into her public service in Portsmouth and medical-research advocacy on the trail. Still, her family name helped her build an early polling lead and bank financial support . Nearly $740,000 raised by Shaheen’s campaign came from donors who had previously given to her mother — 39 percent of total itemized campaign dollars, according to a POLITICO analysis. One of those donors told POLITICO the senator reached out last fall seeking their support for her daughter. Sullivan, Shaheen’s main rival, attempted to weaponize the scion’s family ties in a year where the Democratic base has repeatedly spurned candidates with a perceived connection to the establishment. The primary grew acrimonious in its closing weeks as Shaheen and Sullivan tangled over campaign donations and aired attack ads as polls showed a tightening race. The contest also underwent a rapid winnowing toward the end as two candidates dropped out; one, progressive Christian Urrutia, endorsed Shaheen .

stories.headline: Republicans gather for a Trump-centered midterm convention in Dallas

sources.body: President Donald Trump will be at the center of this week’s GOP midterm convention. Many of his fellow Republicans are hoping he doesn’t make it all about him. The parade of lawmakers, candidates, donors and party officials now headed to Dallas for the two-day spectacle are counting on Trump to make a compelling pitch on the national stage before voters hit the polls. According to interviews with dozens of Republicans, they are largely hoping for a two-pronged approach aimed at getting the president’s committed supporters off the sidelines: a focus on what they call Democrats’ extreme positions and the accomplishments of the Republican Congress — most of which are now more than a year old. “Communism vs. common sense,” Rep. Riley Moore (R-W.Va.) said in an interview, calling the event a “scene-setter” that should stay laser-focused on “what’s on the line” for voters in the election. Republicans have reasons to be wary. Trump’s approval ratings are at record lows for his time in office, and many swing-district GOP lawmakers are torn between running from an unpopular president and alienating his base of committed supporters. There is little evidence Trump is content to let rank-and-file Republicans run away from him. The first pair of national midterm ads funded by his cash-rich political operation put Trump at the very center. One ad begins with businessman Dana White extolling Trump as “the toughest, most resilient person that I've ever met.” The other is more up congressional Republicans’ alley, with a Trump voiceover running through a litany of tax cuts included in last year’s “One Big Beautiful Bill.” Even if not all agree Trump is the party’s best spokesperson at this point, they are eager to see a new effort to promote the tax cuts, which were enacted in July 2025, and want to see them touted anew in Dallas. “It's incredibly important that we highlight what we've accomplished,” Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R-Wis.) said in an interview. “That's the perfect venue for that.” “It's a great opportunity for us to brag about what the Republican Party has done the last year and a half,” added Rep. Craig Goldman (R-Texas). “So certainly talking about the One Big Beautiful Bill.” While Van Orden and Goldman are attending the convention, which kicks off Wednesday and ends Thursday, many other lawmakers and candidates are staying back in their districts . Some of those Republicans said they have scheduling conflicts or simply want to campaign back home. But there are also qualms about Trump’s obsession with priorities that many of them consider off-message ahead of the midterms — such as pressuring Congress to take up the GOP elections bill known as the SAVE America Act. As GOP lawmakers begged Trump to get serious about tackling the high cost of living, the president has instead openly scoffed at “affordability” as an issue concocted by Democrats to hurt Republicans. He refused for months to help pass a major legislative package over the summer designed to help lower housing costs, and his trade wars and ongoing conflict with Iran have contributed to persistent inflation. A recent import deal designed to address rising beef prices came at the cost of upsetting American cattlemen. Speaker Mike Johnson brushed off a question last week about the risk of having candidates show up at a Trump-focused event given his disapproval ratings. “It was the president's idea, which is why he's getting credit for it, and it's rightfully so,” Johnson said. “I think it's going to be an extraordinary opportunity for us to get a couple of nights on national television to talk about our extraordinary record of achievement.” Other Republicans said the president was well positioned to send a message of “promises made, promises kept.” “Politics 101 is just telling folks what you're going to do, and then come to Washington and do it, and then go back and tell them what you did,” said Rep. Mark Harris (R-N.C.). “When you look at President Trump's agenda, securing the border, we've done that. That he wanted to make the tax cuts permanent, we've done that.” “Peace through strength — and I think we have moved in that direction,” he added. “Obviously, we got detoured to this journey over in Iran.” If there is one consensus message Republicans want the convention oriented around, it’s the choice between the legislative record Trump will be touting and a Democratic Party that they argue has moved way too far to the left — especially as progressive candidates, some of them democratic socialists, continue to win key primaries. Rep. Brian Jack (R-Ga.), a deputy chair of the House GOP campaign arm, said “you're going to see on full display each night a contrast that we've never seen before in politics.” “You've got Republicans that are campaigning on commonsense ideas. You've got Democrats that are being drawn to the absolute most extreme left of their party,” he said. “So I expect each night to see that on full display.” RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre also said in a statement that the event would “put front and center Democrats' desire to abolish police and prisons, raise costs, and strip away our freedoms,” while also promoting “Republicans’ historic achievements.” “The Democratic Party has taken a turn for the worse recently,” added Rep. Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.), who is in a competitive race and not attending the convention. “America needs to be quite aware of that as they make their decision here in November.” LaLota is just one of scores of Republican members who are choosing not to travel to the convention — which has a price tag of $25,000 and up for lawmakers attending — but who have an interest in how the event goes off and what impression it gives voters. Rep. Morgan Griffith (R-Va.) called the midterm convention — the first held since Democrats did them in the late 1970s and early 1980s — “an interesting concept” and said he would be paying close attention to the size of the television audience. But he said he would be back in his safe red district campaigning. “I'm going to look forward to listening to it on the radio as I'm driving down the road, going from one spot in my district to another,” he said. Jordain Carney and Meredith Lee Hill contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Republicans are hoping ‘Trump-a-palooza’ isn’t only about Trump

El president dels Estats Units es juga a les eleccions legislatives del 3 de novembre la continuïtat d'aquell moviment tan personalista que els mitjans de comunicació hem anomenat trumpisme.

Sí, és habitual que uns comicis de mig mandat perjudiquin electoralment el partit que ostenta el poder , en aquest cas els republicans.

Però tenint en compte que l'índex de popularitat de Donald Trump es troba sota mínims i que les enquestes auguren una escombrada dels demòcrates (amb més o menys intensitat depenent del sondeig i de l'escó en joc), s'entén ràpidament la idea que el president s'ha tret de la màniga.

Trump ha triat l'American Airlines Center , un gran estadi de Dallas amb capacitat per a 20.000 persones (que els últims 25 anys ha acollit des de finals de l'NBA fins a concerts de grans estrelles del pop) per muntar un xou inèdit en la història del Partit Republicà: una convenció nacional, a l'estil de la prèvia a unes eleccions presidencials, per esperonar la mobilització de les seves bases de cara als comicis de la tardor.

La trobada s'allargarà dos dies (9 i 10 de setembre) i comptarà amb la participació de més de cent personalitats del Partit Republicà .

Hi faran discursos destacats membres del gabinet de Trump, com el vicepresident J. D. Vance, que parlarà dimecres a la nit, o el secretari del Tresor, Scott Bessent; i també alts representants del partit al Congrés, com el líder de la majoria a la Cambra de Representants, Mike Johnson.

I evidentment hi parlarà el president dels Estats Units, que ha promès per enèsima vegada que aquest serà el míting més gran de la història. Donald Trump té previst intervenir els dos dies de congrés. Això li donarà un pes i una presència que farà encara més difícil no llegir les pròximes eleccions com un plebiscit als seus primers dos anys de mandat .

Aquesta omnipresència del president posa en una situació incòmoda alguns dels republicans que es juguen el seu escó en aquestes eleccions, atrapats entre la lleialtat al líder implacable i el votant empipat , que podria decidir aquesta vegada castigar els candidats considerats "trumpistes".

A més, cal tenir present que el president té encara molts diners pendents de gastar en aquesta campanya electoral. L'organització de recaptació de fons MAGA Inc. disposa de 400 milions de dòlars a punt per invertir en candidats que el líder republicà decideixi que són dignes del seu suport.

Quan falten menys de dos mesos per als comicis, la popularitat del president Trump es troba al 38% , el nivell més baix en tot el seu segon mandat .

La decisió de llançar una guerra contra l'Iran amb objectius i resultats poc concrets (un 64% dels nord-americans considera que va ser un error), la pujada del preu del combustible des de l'inici de l'ofensiva (aquesta setmana el preu del dièsel ha assolit un nou rècord i s'ha elevat fins als 5,90 dòlars per galó) i la inflació derivada de la crisi (l'índex interanual el mes de juliol passat es va situar al 3,4%, lluny del 2% recomanat per la Reserva Federal) han disparat la impopularitat del líder republicà que, de sobte, es troba immers en una de les guerres interminables que ell mateix va prometre evitar si tornava a la Casa Blanca.

stories.headline: Spain's Supreme Court suspends voting rights for beneficiaries of the nationality-by-descent law

sources.body:
El Tribunal Supremo ha decido suspender de manera cautelar la inscripción en el Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) de las personas que obtuvieron la nacionalidad española a raíz de la Ley de Memoria Democrática, popularmente conocida como 'ley de nietos', salvo que acrediten su condición de descendientes de españoles que sufrieron exilio por la Guerra Civil y la dictadura franquista.

Mediante una decisión a la que ha tenido acceso RTVE, la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo acuerda suspender la posibilidad de inscribirse en el censo y votar a estas personas en los sucesivos procesos electorales que puedan convocarse, estimando parcialmente las medidas cautelares pedidas por Vox e Iustitia Europa. Te explicamos el origen de esta decisión y sus consecuencias.

“ 🔴 El Supremo paraliza la inscripción en el censo electoral de aquellas personas que obtuvieron la nacionalidad española a raíz de la ley de nietos ▪️ El Alto Tribunal atiende la medida cautelar solicitada por Iustitia Europa, paralizado el derecho a voto para las elecciones… pic.twitter.com/FV2LK1oAqD “

La llamada ' ley de nietos' es el nombre con el que se conoce una disposición adicional de la Ley de Memoria Democrática . Permite obtener la nacionalidad a los nacidos fuera de España de padres o abuelos españoles que la perdieron tras sufrir exilio por "razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia o de orientación e identidad sexual ". También, los hijos nacidos en el exterior de mujeres españolas "que perdieron su nacionalidad por casarse con extranjeros antes de la entrada en vigor de la Constitución de 1978".

Tras la ley, el Gobierno dictó una instrucción sobre cómo aplicar esta medida en los registros consulares, los encargados de los trámites. En este texto, señaló que "se presumirá la condición de exiliado " a todos los que "salieron de España entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955 ", con la condición de que acrediten esa "salida del territorio español". Es decir, amplió la consideración de exiliados y en esto se apoyan los recurrentes para interpretar que la norma abre la puerta a la obtención generalizada de la nacionalidad y, por tanto, el derecho al voto.

El Supremo suspende la inscripción en el censo de votantes del exterior (CERA) a quienes se acojan a esta denominada ‘ley de nietos’, tanto las que ya están tramitadas como las que están en proceso. No suspende la obtención de la nacionalidad, sino la posibilidad de votar.

Lo que exige el alto tribunal es que se acredite que se logra la nacionalidad española de acuerdo con las exigencias de la ley , "sin haber aplicado la presunción" que se dictó después, la citada instrucción. Es necesario acreditar haber nacido "fuera de España, de padre o madre, abuelo o abuela que originariamente fueran españoles, y que hubieran sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas, o de creencia o de orientación de identidad sexual (…)".

El Supremo ordena por ello a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) que requiera de inmediato sobre ese extremo a los encargados de los registros consulares. Igualmente, ordena a la Oficina de Censo Electoral que proceda al desglose de los expedientes de inscripción censal que procedan de la aplicación directa de los supuestos de exilio recogidos en la ley, y de los aprobados al amparo de la interpretación realizada por la instrucción.
sources.headline: El Supremo suspende cautelarmente la posibilidad de votar a los beneficiarios de la 'ley de nietos'

sources.body:
Feijóo y Abascal, en el pleno del Congreso. / José Luis Roca

Las medidas cautelares adoptadas este martes por el Tribunal Supremo (TS) sobre la llamada 'ley de nietos', como se conoce la disposición de la ley de memoria democrática que afecta a los descendientes de exiliados españoles, han provocado un grito de euforia en la derecha, y al mismo tiempo otro enfrentamiento entre el Partido Popular (PP) y Vox . Ambas formaciones sacaron pecho de la suspensión que el Alto tribunal hace de los efectos electores de esa norma, básicamente la concesión del derecho a voto (el que conlleva la nacionalidad española) para cerca de dos millones de personas que podrían acreditar su condición de descendientes (de ahí la denominación no oficial o coloquial de la norma) de exiliados de la Guerra Civil o de la dictadura franquista.

En las redes sociales el presidente de Vox, Santiago Abascal, felicitó al jefe de la delegación de su partido en el Parlamento Europeo, Jorge Buxadé , y a la senadora y coordinadora jurídica del partido, Marta Castro, quienes llevaron la voz cantante en el recurso a la norma, que también presentó Iustitia Europa. Para el líder de Vox, ambos dirigentes habrían prestado un "gigantesco servicio a España y al sistema democrático". Casi a la vez, y compartiendo una de las noticias periodísticas sobre la resolución del TS, el líder de la oposición, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, sintetizó: "Teníamos razón".

Acompañando el mensaje de su jefe de filas, el vicesecretario de Hacienda del PP, Juan Bravo, afirmó en X: "El Tribunal Supremo da la razón a Feijóo ". La reacción de Buxadé en la misma red social no se hizo esperar, sobre todo por compartir Bravo en su perfil una foto de la resolución judicial, que incluso parecía la misma captura de pantalla que la compartida por el eurodiputado de Vox. Otros dirigentes de la extrema derecha se sumaron al ataque a Bravo, en términos muy duros. El vicepresidente de la Junta de Extremadura, Óscar Fernández , le espetó: "Qué vergüenza, Juan, si estáis silbando. No tienes ningún pudor criatura". La diputada nacional María de Meer fue aún más lejos contra su compañero del PP en la Cámara Baja: "No seas sinvergüenza, Juan".

En otro mensaje con tintes justificatorios, la vicesecretaria de Regeneración Institucional del PP, Cuca Gamarra, elogió el "buen y fundado recurso" de Iusticia Europa y justificó que "una vez planteado y abierta esta vía no hacía necesario que el PP la complementase", señaló sin mencionar en momento alguno a Vox.

La batalla y en el enzarzamiento entre las dos formaciones, que justo este año han vuelto a ser socios en hasta cuatro gobiernos autonómicos de coalición, los de la citada Extremadura, además de Aragón, Castilla y León y Andalucía, se libró en las redes sociales, pero también de manera más soterrada. Unos y otros comunicaron a los medios de una forma u otra su influencia o 'paternidad' de la paralización del TS sobre el derecho al voto para esos descendientes de exiliados, que deberá resolverse en un auto definitivo y con la que el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez ya manifestó su disconformidad. El PP recordó el largo camino de oposición política de Feijóo ante esa 'ley de nietos' , incluso los recursos presentados en su día ante el Tribunal Constitucional (TC), así como el compromiso expresado en varias ocasiones por Feijóo de "derogar" la propia ley de memoria democrática si llega a la Moncloa.

stories.headline: Ceuta migration crisis drives a new confrontation between Spain's government and opposition

El Gobierno afronta este miércoles la primera sesión de control del nuevo curso en el Congreso, una semana después de la comparecencia de Pedro Sánchez sobre la crisis abierta en Ceuta a raíz de la entrada de miles de migrantes del 30 y 31 de julio. La gestión del Ejecutivo, criticada por todo el arco parlamentario hace una semana, ha demostrado según el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo que el futuro político de Sánchez "depende del silencio de demasiadas personas" y por eso, ha dicho, " no es un presidente libre ".

" Si Marruecos canta usted se va ", ha advertido el líder del PP al jefe del Ejecutivo, que le ha preguntado "qué haría si mañana volvieran a entrar 80.000 personas en Ceuta", una crisis migratoria que según Feijóo ha demostrado que "su lealtad está comprometida". Y de nuevo, ha insistido en pedirle a Sánchez un adelanto electoral: "No me responde sobre Marruecos, no me responde sobre las listas negras, ha desprotegido a su país y su país se lo hará pagar. Señoría, ponga fecha y nos vemos en las urnas".

La crisis migratoria centra esta sesión de control al Ejecutivo, en la que se han colado otros asuntos de actualidad, como los malos resultados de España en el informe PISA de la OCDE que se hicieron públicos este martes, los casos de presunta corrupción que afectan al entorno del Gobierno, con la declaración este miércoles de la gerente del PSOE , Ana Fuentes, en el caso Leire Díez, y la lista de periodistas con fichas sobre su ideología elaborada por el Ministerio del Interior.

El líder del PP también ha echado en cara a Sánchez los malos resultados de España en el informe PISA de la OCDE en lectura, matemáticas y ciencias. El resultado del "primer examen" de su política educativa ha sido un "fracaso" del " socialismo educativo " y de su ley, la LOMLOE.

Sánchez ha admitido que los resultados son "de extraordinaria preocupación " en todos los países occidentales y ha defendido la gestión de su Gobierno que ha "multiplicado por dos" la inversión en Educación. Se han destinado "más de 400 millones" en cooperación interterritorial con las comunidades autónomas para "reforzar la comprensión lectora y las matemáticas", el "problema", sin embargo, según el jefe del Ejecutivo, son las comunidades autónomas del PP las que "no ejecutan esos recursos".

Según el jefe del Ejecutivo, en esta legislatura hay dos proyectos de ley fundamentales para reforzar la comprensión lectora son la ley de docentes y ratios por aula y la prohibición de que jóvenes mejores de 16 años puedan acceder a las redes sociales: "Mejorarían la comprensión lectora de nuestros jóvenes, espero contar con el voto del PP ".

El líder de la oposición ha acusado a Sánchez de " manipular el censo " con la ley de nietos , aunque ha dicho, "parece que tampoco le va a salir bien", después de que el Tribunal Supremo haya suspendido cautelarmente la posibilidad de votar a los beneficiarios de la norma.

Sánchez le ha respondido que "el problema" es que no quieren "ciudadanos, no de primera y de segunda sino todos de primera con los mismos derechos y también con el derecho al voto" y le ha echado en cara que el PP y la extrema derecha hayan "cercenado el voto a miles de ciudadanos españoles cuyos padres y madres les obligaron al exilio". "Nos veremos en las urnas y volveremos a ganar", ha asegurado.

“No tenemos nada que esconder y actuamos con transparencia”, advirtió ayer la portavoz del Gobierno, Elma Saiz, después de que el Consejo de Ministros aprobara la desclasificación de “todos” los informes que obran en su poder, e incluso las comunicaciones internas entre distintos departamentos gubernamentales, elaborados desde el 1 de julio hasta el 1 de agosto, sobre la entrada masiva de inmigrantes que se produjo en Ceuta los días 30 y 31 de julio.

Son en torno a 40 documentos de la Policía Nacional, la Guardia Civil, el Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI) y los servicios de información de las Fuerzas Armadas (CIFAS), que está previsto que se hagan públicos hoy al mediodía a través de la página web de la Moncloa, como ya se hizo el pasado febrero con los papeles del 23-F.

Ninguno de estos informes reservados a los que ahora tendrá acceso la ciudadanía afecta por tanto a la seguridad nacional, ya que en su caso el Gobierno solo los remitiría a la comisión de secretos oficiales del Congreso.

Y es que el Ejecutivo insiste en que, al menos por ahora, no hay pruebas que apunten a que las autoridades marroquíes estuvieran detrás del asalto a la frontera española en la ciudad autónoma, pese a que así lo dieran ya por hecho tanto el presidente de Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, como el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo.

“Feijóo haría bien en comportarse como un verdadero líder de la oposición y un hombre de Estado, se colocara al lado del Gobierno con responsabilidad y con prudencia, y dejara de abrazar las teorías conspiranoicas o la desinformación”, demandó Elma Saiz al líder del PP.

“El horizonte temporal para devolver a Ceuta a la normalidad y solucionar esta crisis pasa por la colaboración entre administraciones, y ser un partido de oposición que solo pone palos en las ruedas no ayuda en nada a los ceutíes, en nada”, advirtió. “Le exijo que actúe con responsabilidad y con prudencia, como un partido de oposición que tiene que estar a la altura de lo que la ciudadanía demanda”, señaló la ministra portavoz.

La vicepresidenta segunda del Gobierno, Yolanda Díaz, fue aún más contundente en sus críticas al PP, al acusar a los responsables de esta formación de ser “pirómanos del odio” ante la crisis humanitaria en Ceuta, tras un asalto a la frontera en la que perdieron la vida 141 inmigrantes. “Están fracturando la convivencia en todo el país, por fines electorales a corto plazo”, denunció. “El PP está alimentando a la extrema derecha. Y aunque piense que le da muchos votos a corto, las consecuencias son brutales. No se puede hacer esto por un puñado de votos”, afeó Yolanda Díaz.

Elma Saiz, en todo caso, aseguró que la desclasificación de documentos sobre la crisis de Ceuta, por ahora acotada al período temporal entre el primer día de julio y el primero de agosto, podría no ser la última. “Si hubiera otros documentos que aparecieran, y tuvieran relevancia, también se compartirán”, apuntó. Por ahora, no obstante, el Ejecutivo no ve ninguna prueba que acuse a las autoridades marroquíes de haber alentado el asalto a la frontera en Ceuta. Pero la ministra portavoz reiteró las palabras que ya esgrimió la semana pasada el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez: “Si existen pruebas, se actuará con contundencia”.

El Tribunal Supremo ha decido suspender de manera cautelar la inscripción en el Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) de las personas que obtuvieron la nacionalidad española a raíz de la Ley de Memoria Democrática, popularmente conocida como 'ley de nietos', salvo que acrediten su condición de descendientes de españoles que sufrieron exilio por la Guerra Civil y la dictadura franquista.

Mediante una decisión a la que ha tenido acceso RTVE, la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo acuerda suspender la posibilidad de inscribirse en el censo y votar a estas personas en los sucesivos procesos electorales que puedan convocarse, estimando parcialmente las medidas cautelares pedidas por Vox e Iustitia Europa. Te explicamos el origen de esta decisión y sus consecuencias.

La llamada ' ley de nietos' es el nombre con el que se conoce una disposición adicional de la Ley de Memoria Democrática . Permite obtener la nacionalidad a los nacidos fuera de España de padres o abuelos españoles que la perdieron tras sufrir exilio por "razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia o de orientación e identidad sexual ". También, los hijos nacidos en el exterior de mujeres españolas "que perdieron su nacionalidad por casarse con extranjeros antes de la entrada en vigor de la Constitución de 1978".

Tras la ley, el Gobierno dictó una instrucción sobre cómo aplicar esta medida en los registros consulares, los encargados de los trámites. En este texto, señaló que "se presumirá la condición de exiliado " a todos los que "salieron de España entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955 ", con la condición de que acrediten esa "salida del territorio español". Es decir, amplió la consideración de exiliados y en esto se apoyan los recurrentes para interpretar que la norma abre la puerta a la obtención generalizada de la nacionalidad y, por tanto, el derecho al voto.

El Supremo suspende la inscripción en el censo de votantes del exterior (CERA) a quienes se acojan a esta denominada ‘ley de nietos’, tanto las que ya están tramitadas como las que están en proceso. No suspende la obtención de la nacionalidad, sino la posibilidad de votar.

Lo que exige el alto tribunal es que se acredite que se logra la nacionalidad española de acuerdo con las exigencias de la ley , "sin haber aplicado la presunción" que se dictó después, la citada instrucción. Es necesario acreditar haber nacido "fuera de España, de padre o madre, abuelo o abuela que originariamente fueran españoles, y que hubieran sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas, o de creencia o de orientación de identidad sexual (…)".

El Supremo ordena por ello a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) que requiera de inmediato sobre ese extremo a los encargados de los registros consulares. Igualmente, ordena a la Oficina de Censo Electoral que proceda al desglose de los expedientes de inscripción censal que procedan de la aplicación directa de los supuestos de exilio recogidos en la ley, y de los aprobados al amparo de la interpretación realizada por la instrucción.

Los resultados educativos de España se han desplomado en el informe PISA, la mayor evaluación internacional sobre la educación en la que han participado 760.000 estudiantes de 15 y 16 años de 90 países (30.000 de ellos españoles). Los resultados del país se sitúan en su nivel más bajo desde que participa en la prueba en el año 2000. No es un fenómeno aislado. La caída se ha producido en todos los países del mundo, incluso los que se mantienen en cabecera. La OCDE, la institución integrada por los países desarrollados que organiza la prueba, apunta a una menor disposición al esfuerzo, menor capacidad de concentración y al móvil como causantes de la debacle. El uso de las pantallas afecta a la comprensión lectora, que es la puerta de entrada al resto de conocimientos.

La puntuación de los alumnos españoles se queda en 451 en lectura, 457 en matemáticas, y 477 en ciencias, alejándose del promedio de los países desarrollados, que es de 461, 463, y 482 respectivamente.

España pierde respecto a la edición anterior, del 2022, 23 puntos en comprensión lectora, 16 en matemáticas y 8 en ciencias, las tres competencias analizadas por PISA. Cada 20 puntos en el examen equivalen a un curso escolar. El retroceso es de un curso entero menos en lectura y casi otro en matemáticas en tan solo tres años.

La brecha generacional se va agrandando a pasos agigantados. Los jóvenes que han cumplido 26 años estaban mucho mejor preparados para afrontar la mayoría de edad, las cargas de estudios o trabajo, y la ciudadanía en general que los estudiantes que acaban terminar la ESO. Con el agravante de que ya han finalizado la etapa obligatoria.

El descenso se produce en todas las competencias y para todos los alumnos españoles en la media nacional, siendo la primera vez que empeoran los rendimientos de los jóvenes que tradicionalmente mostraban un buen desempeño. El retroceso de los hijos de familias de rentas medias y altas se da tanto en ciencias como en matemáticas y de forma muy pronunciada en lectura.

Baja también la proporción de alumnos brillantes en todas las materias, algo que sucede también en la media de la OCDE. Finalmente, a todo esto se une el fenómeno de la IA, con un uso más frecuente en España que en otras economías del mundo.

Los jóvenes evaluados en la edición de PISA 2025 nacieron en el 2009, vivieron el confinamiento cuando tenían 11 años y estaban en el último curso de primaria. Por tanto, entraron en la secundaria en los años inmediatamente posteriores a la covid, cruciales en sus aprendizajes y convulsos en cuanto a la organización escolar y el estado de bienestar emocional. En este sentido, el informe registra un dato inquietante como apunte de cambio social. Cuando a los alumnos se les pregunta si su familia se interesa por cómo le ha ido el día responden que no. La ausencia de apoyo familiar percibido, mayor en el resto de países que en España, puede atribuirse también al menor espacio de conversación que dejan los móviles, usados por los adultos, o a la precarización laboral.

Espanya cau de manera acusada en les proves PISA respecte a l'última edició, on el descens ja va ser molt destacat. El retrocés és generalitzat a tot el món i, per primer any a la història, Catalunya no té dades comparables perquè la mostra ha estat invalidada.

Coincidint amb l'inici del curs escolar, aquest dimarts s'han publicat els resultats de l'últim informe PISA amb les pitjors dades de la història per a Espanya des que es va començar a fer aquest estudi, l'any 2000. Són unes proves que l'OCDE fa cada tres anys als alumnes de 15 anys en tres competències essencials: lectura, matemàtiques i ciències.

No hi participen tots els centres: els tria la mateixa OCDE amb una mostra aleatòria i els centres poden descartar alguns alumnes que encaixin amb els criteris d'exclusió, com el desconeixement de la llengua o discapacitats cognitives o conductuals.

En aquesta edició s'ha posat el focus en la competència científica, on Espanya perd vuit punts. El descens encara és més pronunciat en matemàtiques (-16), però la patacada més preocupant és en comprensió lectora. Aquí, Espanya perd 23 punts i es distancia de la mitjana dels països de l'OCDE.

En aquest sentit, l'organisme considera que un descens de 20 punts equival a perdre un curs escolar sencer .

Aquest any, l'informe deixa fora Catalunya per un "alt percentatge d'alumnat exclòs (23,2%)", molt superior al límit del 5% establert per l'OCDE. El Ministeri d'Educació, però ha decidit publicar les dades per separat i amb una advertència que diu que "no es poden comparar ni amb els de la resta de territoris ni amb els d'edicions anteriors".

Tot i que els resultats no són comparables , ja que no se sap quines puntuacions obtindrien la resta de comunitats autònomes si haguessin exclòs de la mostra un 23,2% dels alumnes, Catalunya se situa per sobre la mitjana europea i espanyola.

A Espanya, el percentatge d'alumnat exclòs és del 7,89% . Tot i superar el límit, l'OCDE considera vàlides les dades: "Després de fer una anàlisi del biaix, les dades d'Espanya poden ser utilitzades sense restriccions."

A més a més de Catalunya, Múrcia també té una xifra d'exclusió especialment alta (12,7%). A diferència de Catalunya, l'informe sí que inclou els resultats de Múrcia, però demana "que s'interpretin amb cautela pel possible risc de biaix".

Tue Halgreen , responsable de l'avaluació internacional de l'OCDE, apunta que el descens global dels resultats va començar l'any 2015, moment en què els telèfons mòbils "van passar de ser un dispositiu que només tenia una minoria a ser una cosa que a l'abast de la gran majoria de la gent, de tothom".

En les tres matèries analitzades, els resultats a Espanya continuen la forta tendència a la baixa dels últims anys.

Si ens fixem en matemàtiques , els alumnes espanyols s'han distanciat de la mitjana de l'OCDE i han perdut 16 punts respecte a l'edició anterior, mentre que la nota a Espanya és de 457 punts, el Japó, el país líder en les tres matèries, en té 525. La davallada a Espanya, segons l'OCDE, equivaldria a perdre gairebé un curs en aquesta matèria.

stories.headline: Catalonia's Mossos police chief Trapero resigns; Sílvia Catà will become the force's first woman chief

Josep Lluís Trapero ha dimitit de director general dels Mossos d'Esquadra després de dos anys al càrrec, segons ha avançat La Vanguardia i ha confirmat 3CatInfo.

En una compareixença davant els mitjans, la consellera d'Interior, Núria Parlon, ha destacat que Trapero plega per una "decisió personal" . Segons Parlon, Trapero li va comunicar la seva decisió a finals d'agost i, malgrat que la consellera li va manifestar que volia que continués , la decisió del director era "irrevocable":

M'hauria agradat que acabés el mandat, he insistit en què volia que continués.

La consellera ha defugit entrar en valoracions sobre els motius de la decisió : "No entraré en especulacions sobre relacions personals". Parlon ha insistit que només té paraules "de reconeixement i d'agraïment" cap al director general, que comptava tant amb la seva confiança com amb la del president de la Generalitat:

Ha col·locat els Mossos d'Esquadra en un dels seus millors moments professionals.

Ferran López , fins ara al capdavant de la delegació de la policia catalana a Madrid, serà el nou director general dels Mossos en substitució de Trapero. López va ser el cap dels Mossos durant l'aplicació del 155 , després que l'executiu de Mariano Rajoy anunciés el cessament per decret de Josep Lluís Trapero. López va presentar la renúncia al càrrec el 2018 , pocs mesos després d'haver estat nomenat.

El seu nomenament es farà efectiu a partir de dimarts que ve, 15 de setembre.

La dimissió de Trapero arriba només dos anys després del seu nomenament com a màxim responsable polític del cos. La seva direcció ha estat marcada per la lluita contra la multireincidència, amb el pla Kanpai , o l'augment de la presència d' armes blanques i armes de foc als carrers.

També ha hagut de fer front als debats sobre la infiltració de mossos en les assemblees de diferents escoles durant les vagues docents del curs 2025-2026 o la iniciativa d'introduir mossos a les escoles .

Durant la compareixença s'espera que Parlon anunciï més canvis a la cúpula dels Mossos d'Esquadra , ja que l'actual comissari en cap, Miquel Esquius, es jubila. Esquius va assumir el càrrec de cap del cos fa també dos anys, quan Trapero va ser nomenat director general.

La nova comissària en cap dels Mossos serà Sílvia Catà, que es convertirà en la primera dona que ocupa aquest càrrec. Fins ara, Catà ocupava el càrrec de comissària de la regió policial de Girona.

Abans de la compareixença de la consellera d'Interior, el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, i Parlon han mantingut una reunió amb López i amb Catà.

El sindicat de Mossos USPAC assegura que ha rebut els canvis a la cúpula policial amb "sorpresa". En una entrevista a "El matí de Catalunya Ràdio", Fermin Gallart ha assegurat en nom d'aquest sindicat que estan a l'expectativa de veure si els relleus suposen "continuïtat o començar de zero".

"Amb l'arribada de Trapero se'ns havia marcat un pla estratègic fins al 2030 , fins ara ningú no havia vingut amb les idees tan clares. Ara veurem si tot això es perd o es continua en la mateixa direcció", ha explicat Gallart.
sources.headline: Trapero plega com a director dels Mossos i Parlon diu que és una decisió personal: "No entraré en especulacions"

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) El director general dels Mossos d’Esquadra , Josep Lluís Trapero , ha presentat aquest dimecres la dimissió com a director general de la Policia després de dos anys en el càrrec, segons ha avançat La Vanguardia i ha confirmat el Departament d’Interior. Precisament, la consellera d’Interior, Núria Parlon , ha convocat aquest dimecres la prefectura per comunicar els canvis que es produiran en l’organigrama , tenint en compte que el comissari en cap, Miquel Esquius , es jubila. També et pot interessar Parlon confirma Trapero com a director dels Mossos d’Esquadra Redacció 3 minuts de lectura El Departament d’Interior ha confirmat que Ferran López serà el director de la Policia —també destacat per ser mediador en el procés i que ara forma part de la prefectura— i continuarà el llegat a partir del 15 de setembre. Pel que fa al càrrec de Miquel Esquius, ha anunciat que el relleu serà Sílvia Catà . Fins ara, Catà era comissària de la Regió Policial de Girona i serà la primera dona a ocupar aquest càrrec . Deixa el càrrec per voluntat pròpia Interior afirma que Trapero deixa el càrrec per voluntat pròpia després d’aquests dos anys. Per això, Parlon li agraeix la tasca desenvolupada, així com la vocació de servei públic. De fet, a la compareixença ha deixat clar que ha estat una decisió “personal i irrevocable” , i també ha assegurat que la relació entre el Departament i els Mossos ha estat bona durant aquests anys. Així, no creu que les discrepàncies que han sorgit en aquesta etapa “siguin les que han portat a la decisió”. Ha insistit que només hi ha “ paraules d’agraïment ” cap a Trapero i Esquius, i que ara “ els llistons estan alts “. Ara bé, Trapero no marxarà del tot, ja que continuarà ocupant un càrrec a la Comissaria d’Avaluació i està previst que formi part de la Prefectura. Aposta per la feminització del cos Amb Catà com a nova comissària en cap, han sorgit els dubtes sobre si ara s’apostarà per una feminització del cos . Segons Parlon, “podria haver estat també un comissari”, però és conscient que el nou nom té una rellevància simbòlica . De fet, ha recordat que la feminització del cos està impregnant i que en la propera promoció el percentatge de dones ja supera el 40 %: “La idea és assemblar-se el més possible a la societat”. stories.headline: Torrential-rain alert disrupts schools, rail service and flights in Barcelona and surrounding counties

sources.body:
Las fuertes lluvias y tormentas han puesto en alerta este miércoles a Cataluña, que ha restringido la movilidad, ha suspendido clases y ha pedido aplicar el teletrabajo en cinco comarcas. Se trata de las regiones barcelonesas del Baix Llobregat, Vallès Occidental, Garraf y Alt Penedès , así como la tarragonesa del Baix Penedès , cuyos vecinos han recibido un día antes un ES-Alert avisando de la previsión y las medidas.

Esta madrugada el agua ya ha caído con fuerza en en puntos del litoral de las comarcas del Garraf y Baix Llobregat, Barcelona, pero el subdirector de programas de Protecció Civil de la Generalitat, Sergio Delgado, ha alertado de que se "pueden reactivar a lo largo de la mañana" . En una entrevista en '3Cat', ha asegurado que la previsión apunta a que se pueden provocar "daños localmente importantes", por lo que se deben mantener las medidas de precaución.

El Servicio Meteorológico de Cataluña ha alertado, a su vez, de posibilidad de "intensidad torrencial" y de que las precipitaciones puedan estar acompañados de "fenómenos de tiempo violento".

En una rueda de prensa, la consellera de Interior, Núria Parlon, justificó el martes estas medidas restrictivas, que también incluyen suspender la actividad sanitaria no urgente y la de centros de acogida diurna para ancianos y personas con discapacidad mental.

El aeropuerto Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat ha registrado unas 30 cancelaciones de vuelos debido a las tormentas caídas de primera hora, que también han obligado a desviar dos vuelos a Madrid.

Lo ha explicado Aena en una publicación en la red X, en la que detalla que el aeropuerto, que tiene previstas un total de 1.036 operaciones para esta jornada , recupera progresivamente la actividad. No obstante, asegura, que se irá adaptando a la evolución.

Además, se han registrado retrasos en la línea de alta velocidad entre Madrid y Barcelona por una incidencia ocasionada por el temporal, posiblemente por un rayo , que afecta al suministro eléctrico entre Sant Vicenç dels Horts y El Prat de Llobregat, Barcelona.

Adif ha indicado en X de que el personal de la compañía está trabajando para solucionar la incidencia "a la mayor brevedad posible". Las primeras previsiones apuntan a partir de las 13 horas. Fuentes del Ministerio de Transportes han explicado que el corredor está operando actualmente con una vía única por tener la catenaria cortada en ese punto y apuntan a un rayo como posible causa.

En cuanto a los trenes regionales, según informa Renfe, las condiciones meteorológicas adversas han llevado a que los vehículos ferroviarios limiten la velocidad en diversos tramos de las líneas de Rodalies R13, R14, R15, R16, R17, RT1 y RT2.

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) mantiene activada la alerta naranja (riesgo alto) por lluvias y tormentas en la comunidad hasta al menos las 14:00 horas . Las precipitaciones acumuladas pueden alcanzar los 100 mm en solo 3-4 horas , añade. Y en algunos casos, pueden llevar asociados granizo y rachas de viento muy fuertes asociadas. El episodio conlleva, asimismo, una bajada generalizada de las temperaturas, que descenderán entre cinco y diez grados en toda Cataluña.

Una avaria derivada del temporal de pluja a Catalunya ha obligat a tallar la circulació de trens d'altra velocitat entre Barcelona i Madrid durant dues hores.

Les pluges al litoral central han causat una avaria a la catenària de Sant Vicenç dels Horts, la qual ha obligat els trens a circular per via única en el tram comprès entre el Prat de Llobregat i Gelida, provocant retards superiors a l'hora.

Per tal de solucionar la problemàtica i imperir més endarreriments, s'ha decidit tallar la circulació de trens AVE fins a la una del migdia. Una mesura que Adif justifica com a necessària pel fet que els treballs de reparació requereixen tallar la tensió elèctrica.

Aquesta és la conseqüència del temporal més important registrada, fins ara, a Catalunya.

Les pluges han descarregat aquest dimecres a primera hora a les cinc comarques on hi havia avisos de perill molt alt per pluja intensa, l'Alt Penedès, el Baix Penedès, el Garraf, el Baix Llobregat i el Vallès Occidental.

A banda, les precipitacions han provocat incidències a Rodalies i a l'aeroport del Prat. A mig matí, però, les precipitacions s'han desplaçat cap al Ripollès , al Berguedà i a la Garrotxa.

Tot i això, es mantenen les restriccions a les comarques del litoral central on es van establir les alertes, en les quals la Generalitat ha suspès l'activitat educativa i ha demanat prioritzar el teletreball. Es preveu ue es mantinguin fins, com a mínim, les 5 de la tarda.

A les sis del matí ha començat a ploure amb força al Garraf . Seguidament, Els ruixats de seguida han avançat cap al Penedès, al Baix Llobregat i al Vallès Occidental.

🌧️ Les pluges fortes ja han començat. Al Garraf es concentra ara mateix la zona de màxima intensitat, i la precipitació comença a arribar al Baix Llobregat i també es comença a activar al Penedès. 📍 Vilanova i la Geltrú — 06.00 h 📸 Erik Tarazona https://t.co/uG11dPB1qj pic.twitter.com/PcUTyAabZv

A les 10 del matí, les precipitacions més importants s'han registrat a Sitges, al Garraf, on han caigut 47 litres per metre quadrat, seguit de Borredà, al Berguedà, amb 45.

Malgrat que les pluges s'han desplaçat cap al nord-est a mig matí, segueixen vigents les restriccions al Garraf, Penedès, Baix Llobregat i Vallès Occidental –on s'han suspès aquest dimecres les classes i l'activitat esportiva a l'aire lliure i es recomana el teletreball– es mantindran davant la possibilitat que tornin les fortes pluges de primera hora. Tot i això, des de Protecció Civil es preveu que les limitacions decaiguin a les 5 de la tarda.

En aquest sentit, Inma Solé, subdirectora general de Coordinació i Gestió d'Emergències ha defensat les alertes, tot i que admet que són "una eina nova, que ha d'evolucionar".

Segons el subdirector de programes de Protecció Civil, Sergio Delgado, en declaracions al programa Matins, encara hi ha perill de "tempestes fortes que puguin provocar danys localment importants".

Es mantenen les mesures perquè les tempestes es poden reactivar durant el matí.

Delgado ha justificat aquestes mesures preventiva perquè venim de temperatures molt elevades, també al mar.

La Comissió Europea planteja restringir el lloguer turístic i la compra de segones residències en zones de mercat tensionat per fer front a la crisi de l'habitatge.

El govern comunitari proposa criteris comuns arreu de la Unió Europea per delimitar quan es pot considerar que una zona està tensionada.

És el que dibuixa l'esborrany de la nova llei d'habitatge assequible , al qual ha tingut accés 3CatInfo, que la Comissió Europea presentarà aquest dimecres.

És el primer cop que Brussel·les empara, a escala europea, la possibilitat de restringir la compra o el lloguer de pisos, amb l'objectiu que només siguin utilitzats com a primeres residències.

Amb aquesta norma, la Comissió Europea pretén delimitar el terreny de joc als estats, regions o ajuntaments que vulguin intervenir el mercat de l'habitatge.

Els dona més cobertura legal , tenint en compte que aquesta qüestió sovint acaba als tribunals per les denúncies de particulars o d'actors que hi estan en contra.

Però, d'una altra banda, també fixa condicions per poder regular l'habitatge.
sources.headline: Crisi de l'habitatge: Brussel·les vol restringir el lloguer turístic i la compra de segones residències
